title: How to get started with Bitcoin self-custody (River)
plain: Self-custody means you, not a company, control the secret keys to your bitcoin. Keys are codes: a private key is the secret code that lets money move, and an address is where money gets sent. Whoever holds the keys controls the coins — people shorten this to 'not your keys, not your coins.' River, a Bitcoin company, teaches self-custody because it removes counterparty risk, the chance that a company holding your money fails, gets robbed, or blocks you, and it improves privacy. Pick a wallet by how much money is involved. For $1 to $300, a mobile app wallet is fine; think pocket money. For $300 to $75,000, use a hardware wallet: a small gadget that keeps keys offline, like a home safe. For $75,000 or more, use multisig, short for multisignature — a wallet that needs several keys to agree before money moves, like a guarded vault. River's walkthrough uses a phone app called Blue Wallet. Set it up privately at home, away from cameras. A wallet on an internet-connected phone is called a hot wallet; it suits learning and small amounts, not savings. The most important idea is the seed phrase: 12 or 24 ordinary words that stand for one huge random number. Every address and private key grows out of that number, so those words are the money. Write them on paper, in the exact order shown. Check twice. Wrong spelling or word order likely means your bitcoin cannot be recovered. Never type seed words into anything connected to the internet, and never share them with anyone. Then practice safely. Send a tiny test payment to your new address. Wait about an hour, if the fee was normal, for 6 confirmations — a confirmation is one new block of payment records added by miners, the computers that run Bitcoin. Then, only after re-checking your paper copy against the screen, delete the wallet and restore it by typing your words back in. If the money reappears, your backup works. Your words would also restore the money in any other wallet app, even if this one disappears.
technical: River's guide advocates self-custody — user-managed public/private key pairs — to reduce counterparty risk, increase censorship resistance, and enhance privacy. Wallet selection is by dollar value: mobile, browser, or desktop hot wallets for $1-$300; single-signature hardware wallets for $300-$75,000; multisignature setups for $75,000 or more. The walkthrough uses Blue Wallet on mobile. Step 1: install only from official app stores; enable the optional app PIN in Security settings. Step 2: create an on-chain Bitcoin wallet and transcribe the 12-word seed phrase — the large random number from which all addresses, private keys, and signatures derive — to paper, verifying exact spelling and word order; never store it on internet-connected devices. Step 3: receive a low-value test transaction (River's minimum withdrawal: 0.0001 BTC), sharing the address via encrypted messaging such as Signal; cross-check the recommended fee at mempool.space; 6 confirmations is treated as final settlement, roughly 1 hour at adequate fees. Step 4: after re-verifying the written seed via Export/Backup, delete the wallet — the app requires entering the current balance to confirm — then re-import the seed in lowercase with single spaces; the wallet imports as 'Imported HD SegWit...' and the seed is portable to any other wallet software. Step 5: before broadcasting, verify amount, recipient address (compare first and last six characters), and fee. Caveats: Blue Wallet is a hot wallet unsuited to large savings; never buy refurbished hardware wallets; monitor vendor firmware updates; a 2-of-3 multisig backup requires at least two of three seed backups plus all three xpubs (extended public keys); assisted multisig providers (Unchained, Casa, Nunchuk) hold one key while the user holds two and retains unilateral exit; seedless products like Bitkey spread control across devices or trusted contacts.

claims.claim: Self-custody means the user personally manages the public/private key pairs for their bitcoin, and whoever controls the keys ultimately controls the bitcoin.
claims.source: Intro: 'By self-custody, we mean that you are the person responsible for managing the public/private key pairs' and 'whoever controls your keys, ultimately controls your bitcoin.'

claims.claim: River recommends self-custody because it reduces counterparty risk, increases censorship resistance, and enhances privacy.
River's five-step self-custody walkthrough takes about 30 minutes.
claims.source: Intro: 'the five steps outlined below, which should take about 30 minutes.'

claims.claim: River's recommended wallet thresholds: mobile, browser, or desktop wallets for $1-$300; single-signature hardware wallets for $300-$75,000; multisignature hardware setups for $75,000 or more.
A seed phrase is a very large number from which all addresses, private keys, and signatures are derived, represented as 12 or 24 words because that format is easier for humans.
Wallet software does not control bitcoin; funds can only be moved with private keys, so a backed-up seed phrase preserves access even if the wallet software is discontinued.
claims.source: 'What are seed phrases?' section and Key Takeaways.

claims.claim: If seed words are written down incorrectly or in the wrong order, the bitcoin likely cannot be recovered.
Seed phrases should not be stored on any internet-connected device; paper backups are preferred and multiple copies are advised.
The minimum withdrawal amount from River's wallet is 0.0001 BTC.
Six confirmations is the general rule for final settlement, taking roughly 1 hour if the wallet set an appropriate transaction fee.
Recommended fee rates can be cross-checked at mempool.space or another block explorer.
Blue Wallet is a hot wallet and should not be used to store large amounts of bitcoin savings.
A seed phrase generated in Blue Wallet can be imported into any other wallet software.
Never buy a refurbished or second-hand hardware wallet; buy directly from the manufacturer to avoid tampered devices.
Backing up a 2-of-3 multisig setup requires maintaining at least two of the three seed backups plus all three signers' xpubs.
With assisted multisig, the user holds two keys and the service provider holds one, and the user can exit the wallet unilaterally without the provider's permission.
Bitkey (by Block) is a seedless custody product that distributes control across multiple devices or trusted contacts, so losing a single device does not mean losing access.
Hardware wallet vendors periodically discover bugs or vulnerabilities; users should monitor vendor social media or GitHub and update when fixes are released.

warnings: Never delete your wallet until you have verified that your written seed phrase exactly matches the seed shown on screen — every word spelled correctly and in the correct order.
Never store, type, or photograph your seed words on any internet-connected device, and never share them with anyone.
Never buy a refurbished or second-hand hardware wallet — buy only directly from the manufacturer.
Do not create or back up a wallet in public or within view of cameras or windows.

notes_for_reviewer: 1) The cached text contains no self-URL or publication date; source_url is inferred from River's learn-center URL pattern and must be verified before shipping. 2) Dollar thresholds ($1-$300 / $300-$75,000 / $75,000 or more), the 'over $75k consider multisig' guidance, and the 0.0001 BTC River minimum withdrawal are River's editorial figures and may have changed since publication. 3) Blue Wallet UI details (the '...' menu, Security/PIN toggle, Export/Backup flow, deletion requiring the current balance, 'Imported HD SegWit' wallet name) reflect the app at time of writing; verify against the current app version. 4) '6 confirmations in approximately 1 hour' is fee- and network-dependent; the source itself hedges ('as a general rule', 'should'). 5) The claim that a Blue Wallet seed imports into 'any other wallet software' is stated without derivation-path or address-type caveats; treat as the source's assertion, not a protocol guarantee. 6) Vendor and product mentions (Unchained, Casa, Nunchuk, Bitkey, SeedSigner, Foundation Passport, Blockstream Jade, BitBox02, Trezor, Ledger) will go stale; re-verify if this entry links out to them. 7) The seedless section contains a typo ('wolutions') and reads promotional; Bitkey claims carry the vendor's marketing framing. 8) The source references an embedded Andreas M.
